A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPARTAN. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Retained content can be matched across the changed title and reorganized sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction, graph discovery, robustness, and adaptation experiments on Interventional Pong, CREATE, and Traffic, together with training analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds ACD baseline comparisons in Table 7 and learned-object-representation experiments in Table 8.

M1.justification: The hard-attention sampling, multilayer path regularization, intervention tokens, adaptation procedure, and Lagrangian training remain unchanged. Appendix D evaluates learned object representations within the existing factored-input framework; it does not introduce a new SPARTAN component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Interventional Pong, CREATE, and Waymo Traffic, retaining the intervention and scene-composition scenarios in Appendix B and Tables 5–6. The added comparisons reuse these tasks; learned slots change the representation configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C/Table 7 adds one comparator family: adapted Amortised Causal Discovery, evaluated as ACD and Sparse ACD on Pong and CREATE. Existing Transformer/CoDA, Global Graph, and Traffic Local Attention comparisons remain. ELDEN is reported as attempted but unstable, without a scored comparison.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce current-state conditioning for ACD, comparisons using 50% versus ground-truth sparsity priors, and learned-slot Pong evaluation with attention-mask-based object matching for SHD. The original hyperparameters, environment configurations, and five-trajectory adaptation protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D/Table 8 newly tests whether the prediction and graph-learning findings persist with learned slots instead of ground-truth-masked representations. Appendix C also checks whether ACD's disadvantage persists when given the true sparsity prior. Existing robustness, adaptation, and training-curve analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 8 explicitly reports standard errors for prediction error and SHD. v1 already contains uncertainty values and plotted error bars, but does not identify them as standard errors. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their values. New Table 7 reports CREATE SHD of 1.17 for SPARTAN, 39.77 for ACD, and 5.45 for Sparse ACD. Table 8 adds learned-slot Pong results: prediction errors 7.21 versus 6.90 and SHD 2.69 versus 8.52 for SPARTAN versus Transformer. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1's explicit general interventional causal-discovery objective, with separate graph and intervention penalties in Section 2.2/Eq. 3, is omitted in v3. The local-graph definition and SPARTAN mathematics remain equivalent. The Lagrangian formulation is retained in Appendix A.2 rather than removed.

C1.justification: v3 adds an explicit introduction claim that SPARTAN is the first method to learn local causal structures beyond simple state-based settings. Its abstract foregrounds context-dependent interaction structures, while retaining the central claims about accurate graphs, prediction quality, robustness, and efficient adaptation.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly explains that ground-truth masks avoid ambiguous object matching when evaluating SHD, and discusses applicability to pretrained representations. Section 3.2 clarifies that multi-environment intervention modeling is optional. Conversely, v1's qualification that Traffic human labels are subjective qualitative references is omitted. The principal identifiability and adaptation limitations remain.

D1.justification: New appendices document ACD's conditioning and sparsity choices and the attention-mask procedure for matching learned slots to ground-truth objects. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain. Table 1 loses its explicit definitions of token-space L2 prediction error and Traffic average displacement error.

R1.justification: Section 5 and new Appendix C substantially expand positioning against local causal-learning approaches, explaining architectural and scaling constraints for ELDEN, FCDL, CAI, and CoDA and introducing ACD. v3 adds a substantive comparison with the Consciousness Prior and related planning work, while removing the earlier RIM-centered discussion of independent mechanisms.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten. The background is reorganized around a dedicated Local Causal Models subsection, related work is reordered and revised, and the Lagrangian explanation is consolidated in Appendix A. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 7–8, revises the Figure 1 schematic, corrects Figure 4's legend from STRAW to SPARTAN, and resizes or relocates existing displays. Several captions are shortened, and Figure 6 loses its individual panel labels. Most original graphical content and table structures remain.

improvement.justification: The ACD comparisons and learned-slot Pong experiment provide useful additional validation, addressing gaps in v1's comparator coverage and reliance on ground-truth masks. Expanded discussion also clarifies relationships to prior methods. The gains remain limited: learned-slot validation covers only Pong, and run counts remain unspecified. Removing Table 1's metric definitions and the Traffic-label qualification reduces clarity, but the added empirical checks support a modest net improvement.
